item.text:
**Overall:** Lula’s 2024 record on market rules is mixed but leans positive. The strongest positives are fiscal-rule support, central-bank autonomy language, territorial/property regularization, and policies that broadened participation in work and production. The main negatives are credibility-denting fiscal improvisation, persistent deficits, and recurring political pressure on the central bank. I did not find strong evidence of overt anti-competition favoritism or a major collapse in property-rights protection.

- [Lula sends Congress calamity message to exclude RS reconstruction spending from fiscal result](https://economia.uol.com.br/noticias/reuters/2024/05/06/lula-envia-ao-congresso-mensagem-de-calamidade-no-rs-para-excetuar-gastos-de-resultado-fiscal.htm) - Reuters via UOL - 2024-05-06 - Lula sought an emergency exemption for flood reconstruction spending, which is understandable policy-wise but still shows willingness to bypass the fiscal scorecard when politically salient. Question IDs: 5B.4, 5B.3

- [Lula says next central bank chief should look at Brazil, not the financial system](https://noticias.uol.com.br/ultimas-noticias/reuters/2024/07/01/lula-critica-bc-autonomo-e-diz-que-autoridade-monetaria-nao-atende-populacao.htm) - Reuters via UOL - 2024-07-01 - Lula said he respected formal autonomy but also publicly pressured the central bank to be less market-oriented, which is the clearest negative signal on monetary credibility. Question IDs: 5B.4, 5B.3, 5B.2

Search gap: I found limited direct evidence on trade policy, competition policy, and formal investment-law reform in 2024. The picture is therefore driven mostly by fiscal/monetary credibility, property regularization, and broad labor/inclusion measures rather than by a clearly documented competition-reform agenda.
